paras: The lynching of Henry Jones took place near Woodland Mills, in Obion County, Tennessee, on the night of October 26, 1888, when a mob killed Jones, a Black man. A Nashville wire dispatch said he had murdered a white man, while a Kentucky weekly, the Hickman Courier, said he had shot at a man and wounded his horse, and that he was taken from officers and hanged. The two-sentence wire item ran in papers from Virginia to Washington Territory, and no report of an inquest or arrests appears in the coverage.

According to the Nashville dispatch, Jones "had murdered a white man in cold blood Thursday night," that is, on October 25. The wire did not name the man said to have been killed. The Hickman Courier, published in Hickman, Kentucky, gave a different charge: on Thursday night of the previous week, Jones had shot at Tom Golden of Fulton and wounded his horse. The Courier added that Jones, "it is said," bore a bad character and that there was "good proof" he had figured in burning and robbing for years.

Officers had Jones in custody near Troy when he was taken from them, according to the Hickman Courier. His captors brought him back to near Woodland Mills and hanged him. The Nashville dispatch, dated October 27, said only that Jones was "lynched by a mob at Woodland Mills" the night before, and the Salt Lake Herald placed it on Friday night. No report gives the size of the mob or names any of its members.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response was found in the coverage, which ended within two weeks.

Almost all of the coverage derived from one Nashville dispatch, which the Richmond Dispatch, the Memphis Appeal and the Savannah Morning News printed on October 28. The Memphis Appeal headed it "A Lynching In Obion County," the Richmond Dispatch "Lynched," and the St. Paul Daily Globe "Lynched by a Mob." Other papers put the accusation in the headline: the Seattle Post-Intelligencer ran "Negro Murderer Lynched" and the Savannah Morning News "A Murderer Lynched." Every version stated the alleged murder as fact rather than as a charge.

Through the following week the item was condensed into news digests, such as the Clarksville Evening Chronicle's "Pointed Paragraphs" and the Worthington Advance's weekly summary. It was reprinted as far away as Los Angeles, St. Paul and Spokane Falls. In early November a "Southern Gleanings" version appeared in the Brookhaven Leader in Mississippi and the West Tennessee Star of Bolivar. That version said Jones was lynched "a few nights ago" for a murder "a few nights before." Rewriting garbled some details: the Salt Lake Herald put the town in Pennsylvania, and the Middleburgh Post wrote "O'Brien county" and called the lynchers "a mob of white citizens."

The only report not taken from the wire came from the Hickman Courier of Hickman, Kentucky, which gave place names around the scene such as Troy and Fulton. Its account named Tom Golden, reported a wounded horse rather than a killing, and added unattributed claims about Jones's past.

Accounts differ on what Jones was accused of: the Nashville wire said he murdered a white man, while the Hickman Courier said he shot at Tom Golden of Fulton and wounded his horse. Neither account named a source, and no later report settled the question. The date also varies in digests, with the Sacramento Daily Record-Union giving "Saturday night" and the Worthington Advance "the 27th," against the dispatch's "last night" of October 26.

reader.title: Lynching of Henry Jones
bases: A mob killed Henry Jones at Woodland Mills after, by one account, taking him from officers (A2, A3, A20).

Every report says Jones was 'lynched by a mob' (A2, A3, A11), and the Hickman Courier says he was taken from officers and hanged (A20); the stated reason was an alleged crime against a white man (A2, A20).
The Nashville wire (A2, A3) and the separately written Hickman Courier item (A20) agree that Jones was lynched near Woodland Mills, though they differ on his alleged offense.

accounts.label: Nashville wire report
accounts.gist: Henry Jones, a Black man, was lynched by a mob at Woodland Mills, Obion county, on the night of October 26; he 'had murdered a white man in cold blood Thursday night.'

accounts.label: Hickman Courier (Hickman, Ky.)
accounts.gist: Jones had shot at Tom Golden of Fulton and wounded his horse on Thursday night; he was taken from officers near Troy, brought back to near Woodland Mills and hanged; he was 'said' to bear a bad character and to have figured in burning and robbing for years.

framing.detail: Most papers ran the two-sentence Nashville wire, stating as fact that Jones 'had murdered a white man in cold blood', under headlines such as 'Lynched.' and 'A Lynching In Obion County.'
Headlines and digest lines labeled Jones 'a negro murderer' ('Negro Murderer Lynched', 'A Murderer Lynched'), naming the accusation rather than the mob.
The Hickman Courier added unattributed charges that Jones 'bore a bad character' and had long figured in 'burning and robbing'.

conflicts.note: The Hickman Courier, the only account not drawn from the wire, reports no killing; the wire names no victim. Neither version identifies a source.

versions.value: Night of October 26 ('last night' in an Oct. 27 dispatch; 'Friday night')

conflicts.note: The later dates appear in digests that rewrote the Oct. 27 dispatch date; the dispatch itself puts the lynching the night before.
The Pennsylvania and 'O'Brien' versions are evident garbles of the Tennessee wire.
